findings.section: 2c. What the seconds themselves cost
findings.claim: In the calibrated model's own price of time, the player's slower blitz pace costs 0.038 expected points per game more than opponents pay (0.248 vs 0.211).

findings.stake_note: The paired difference in clock charge per blitz game: the model's price of the player's slower pace relative to the opponents'.
findings.caveat: The charge is the model's price of time learnt from these games (gradient boosting, not monotone in the clocks) and not an additive component of ep_loss.

findings.metric: sum over a side's moves of the clock charge, per game
findings.caveat: Both sides spend the whole clock in bullet, so the totals are similar and largely cancel in the game's outcome.

findings.section: 2. Does spending time buy accuracy?
findings.claim: In expected points the player's 8+ s bullet moves lose less than the opponents' (0.1139 vs 0.1362), the opposite sign to cp_loss, because ep_loss also charges the clock and opponents' long thinks are longer.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on moves of 8+ s
findings.caveat: ep_loss charges a move for the clock it consumes (the position after the move is valued with the clock after the move); cp_loss is clock-free.

findings.section: 2. Does spending time buy accuracy?
findings.claim: The player's blitz moves under 1 s lose 0.0023 expected points less per move than the opponents'.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on moves of <1 s
findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.section: 2. Does spending time buy accuracy?
findings.claim: The player's rapid moves of 2-5 s lose 0.0042 expected points less per move than the opponents'.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on moves of 2-5 s
findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.section: 2. Does spending time buy accuracy?
findings.claim: In expected points the player's <0.5 s bullet moves are no different from the opponents' (0.0180 vs 0.0185), although in cp they are cleaner.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on moves of <0.5 s
findings.caveat: ep_loss charges a move for the clock it consumes (the position after the move is valued with the clock after the move); cp_loss is clock-free.

findings.claim: On bullet high-stakes positions played in 0.5-1 s the player loses 0.0095 expected points more per move than opponents.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on high-stakes (0.10+) positions, moves of 0.5-1 s
findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.section: 2a. Within stakes bands
findings.claim: On rapid high-stakes positions played in 2-5 s the player loses 0.0165 expected points less per move than opponents (and -0.0131 [-0.0229, -0.0029] under 2 s).
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on high-stakes (0.10+) positions, moves of 2-5 s
findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.section: 2a. Within stakes bands
findings.claim: On bullet medium-stakes positions played in 8+ s the player loses 0.0126 expected points more per move than opponents (4-8 s: 0.0048 [0.0016, 0.0088]).
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on medium-stakes (0.03-0.10) positions, moves of 8+ s
findings.caveat: Time spent is confounded with difficulty: harder positions get more time, so raw error rises with seconds spent; only the you-vs-opponents comparison within the same cell is robust, not the level.

findings.section: 2b. Adjusted
findings.claim: Holding position features fixed, the player's bullet moves of 8+ s lose 36.1 cp more relative to own snap moves than the opponents' do; the player's error-vs-time gradient is steeper in every bullet bucket (0.5-1 s: 20.9 [17.2, 24.3]).
findings.metric: side x time-bucket interaction in a linear model of cp_loss with stakes, phase, ply, material, clocks, legal moves, check and |eval| as controls; 8+ s vs <0.5 s
findings.caveat: Positive coefficients for both sides mean the controls do not capture difficulty; the coefficients are not the causal value of a second, only the you - opp column is informative.

findings.section: 2b. Adjusted
findings.claim: Holding position features fixed, the player's blitz moves of 20+ s lose 25.5 cp more relative to own snap moves than the opponents' do (10-20 s: 15.5 [9.3, 21.9]).
findings.metric: side x time-bucket interaction in the adjusted cp_loss model; 20+ s vs <1 s
findings.caveat: The coefficients are not the causal value of a second; only the you - opp column is informative.

findings.section: 2b. Adjusted
findings.claim: Holding position features fixed, the player's rapid moves of 20-40 s lose 34.7 cp more relative to own snap moves than the opponents' do; at 40+ s the difference is -12.5 [-39.2, 12.4].
findings.metric: side x time-bucket interaction in the adjusted cp_loss model; 20-40 s vs <2 s
findings.caveat: The coefficients are not the causal value of a second; only the you - opp column is informative.

findings.section: 2b. Adjusted
findings.claim: In expected points the player's adjusted blitz gradient is also steeper: moves of 20+ s cost 0.0097 more relative to snap moves than the opponents' do.
findings.metric: side x time-bucket interaction in the adjusted ep_loss model; 20+ s vs <1 s
findings.caveat: ep_loss charges a move for the clock it consumes (the position after the move is valued with the clock after the move); cp_loss is clock-free.

findings.section: 2b. Adjusted
findings.claim: In rapid the adjusted ep_loss gradient of the player's 2-5 s moves is the same as the opponents' (0.0004 difference).
findings.metric: side x time-bucket interaction in the adjusted ep_loss model; 2-5 s vs <2 s

findings.section: 3. The where-to-spend-time map
findings.claim: In bullet high-stakes endgame positions the player spends 1.45 s per move against the opponents' 1.81 s.
findings.metric: mean seconds spent per move, endgame, ep_criticality 0.10+

findings.section: 3. The where-to-spend-time map
findings.claim: In bullet high-stakes middlegame positions the player spends 3.02 s per move against the opponents' 3.46 s.
findings.metric: mean seconds spent per move, middlegame, ep_criticality 0.10+

findings.section: 3. The where-to-spend-time map
findings.claim: In bullet opening positions with nothing at stake the player spends 1.29 s per move against the opponents' 1.15 s.
findings.metric: mean seconds spent per move, opening, no stakes

findings.section: 3. The where-to-spend-time map
findings.claim: In blitz opening positions with nothing at stake the player spends 4.81 s per move against the opponents' 4.32 s.
findings.metric: mean seconds spent per move, opening, no stakes

findings.section: 3. The where-to-spend-time map
findings.claim: In blitz high-stakes middlegame positions the player's slow moves (3.2 s or more) lose 0.0742 expected points more than the quick ones, opponents' 0.0644; the gap is not the benefit of time because slow moves are the harder ones.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss of slow moves (at or above the class median seconds) minus quick moves, middlegame, ep_criticality 0.10+
findings.caveat: Within a cell the slow moves are still the harder ones, so slow - quick is positive almost everywhere and is not the benefit of time.

findings.section: 3a. The price of having no time
findings.claim: Bullet opening/middlegame high-stakes moves made with under 10 s on the clock lose 117.8 cp more than the same kind of move at 30+ s (opponents 72.8); this is the price of having no time where it is imposed by the game.
findings.metric: mean cp_loss on moves with <10 s on the clock minus moves with 30+ s, opening/middlegame, ep_criticality 0.10+
findings.caveat: In ep the same cell is 0.0275 [0.0117, 0.0443] for you and 0.0346 [0.0177, 0.0534] for opponents; the calibration discounts positional damage when the mover is about to flag.

findings.section: 3a. The price of having no time
findings.claim: Even bullet opening/middlegame moves with nothing at stake lose 62.1 cp more under 10 s than at 30+ s (opponents 52.3), though in expected points the gap is nil (0.0011 [-0.0008, 0.0031]).
findings.metric: mean cp_loss on moves with <10 s minus moves with 30+ s, opening/middlegame, no stakes
findings.caveat: cp_loss is clock-free; the ep version of the same cell straddles zero.

findings.section: 3a. The price of having no time
findings.claim: In bullet endgames with nothing at stake the shortage of time does not separate the moves: 5.6 cp difference between <10 s and 30+ s moves, straddling zero (medium stakes -6.8 [-21.0, 6.2], high stakes -6.4 [-29.3, 18.3]).
findings.metric: mean cp_loss on moves with <10 s minus moves with 30+ s, endgame, no stakes
findings.caveat: The 30+ s moves of a bullet endgame are the early, material-rich endgames, so the comparison is not like for like.

findings.section: 3a. The price of having no time
findings.claim: In blitz high-stakes endgames moves under 10 s lose 0.0169 expected points more than at 30+ s (opponents 0.0195), both wide and straddling zero.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss on moves with <10 s minus moves with 30+ s, endgame, ep_criticality 0.10+
findings.caveat: In cp the same cell is 15.2 [-37.5, 93.1] for you and 22.8 [-30.7, 99.6] for opponents.
